question: A 15-year-old boy is brought to the physician for a well-child visit. His parents are concerned that he has not had his growth spurt yet. As a child, he was consistently in the 60th percentile for height; now he is in the 25th percentile. His classmates make fun of his height and high-pitched voice. His parents are also concerned that he does not maintain good hygiene. He frequently forgets to shower and does not seem aware of his body odor. As an infant, he had bilateral orchidopexy for cryptorchidism and a cleft palate repair. He is otherwise healthy. Vital signs are within normal limits. On physical exam, axillary and pubic hair is sparse. Genitals are Tanner stage 1 and the testicles are 2 mL bilaterally. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Cryptorchidism and cleft palate repair as an infant -> possible underlying genetic condition -> 70% CHAIN: Sparse axillary and pubic hair, Tanner stage 1 genitals, and small testicles -> possible hypogonadism -> 60% CHAIN: Delayed growth spurt, low percentile for height, and high-pitched voice -> possible delayed puberty -> 70% CHAIN: Lack of awareness of body odor and poor hygiene -> possible lack of secondary sexual characteristics -> 60% CHAIN: Overall presentation with delayed puberty, sparse hair, small testicles, and lack of secondary sexual characteristics -> possible Kallmann syndrome -> 70%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis for the 15-year-old boy with delayed puberty, sparse hair, small testicles, lack of secondary sexual characteristics, and history of cryptorchidism and cleft palate repair is Kallmann syndrome. This is supported by the presence of hypogonadism, which can be associated with Kallmann syndrome. The evidence paths confirm the link between hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and Kallmann syndrome, further strengthening this diagnosis.
analysis: The most likely diagnosis for this 15-year-old boy with delayed puberty, sparse hair, small testicles, lack of secondary sexual characteristics, and a history of cryptorchidism and cleft palate repair is Kallmann syndrome. The presence of hypogonadism, specifically hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, aligns with the enhanced information provided, which strongly supports the diagnosis of Kallmann syndrome.
